items.question: What attainment makes one dear to the yoginis?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are sought goals
Great accomplishment is a supreme attainment
Such attainment wins favor with yoginis
items.inference: One who attains great accomplishment in enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: One may become dear to the yoginis through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes after the teaching on Candra-dvipa?
premises: The discourse has emerged from Candra-dvipa
A numbered chapter is being marked
The ordinal indicates sequence
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes after the emergence from Candra-dvipa.
items.plain_english: Thus the ninth chapter, having emerged from Candra-dvipa, is concluded.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire?
premises: The self is imagined as encircled by fire
The posture involves balance on one foot
The visualization specifies a stable stance
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire while standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing firmly on one foot.

items.question: What clarification about knowledge is requested from the deity now?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity directly
A determination of knowledge is sought
The request asks for immediate manifestation
items.inference: The speaker asks the deity to make the determination of knowledge manifest today.
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me today.

items.question: What comprehensive division of eightfold groups is sought to be fully known?
premises: The division consists of eight groups of eight
Complete knowledge of this division is desired
The knowing is described as endless or thorough
items.inference: The aim is to fully and thoroughly know the division of the eight groups of eight.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean endlessly or in infinite detail
items.plain_english: I seek to know fully and thoroughly the division of the eight groups of eight.

items.question: How does the wheel in the secret place bring swift accomplishment?
premises: A secret place is specified
The wheel is located there
Accomplishment occurs quickly
items.inference: The wheel in the secret place accomplishes its result quickly.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel in the secret place is quickly accomplished.

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the Great Goddess for her question?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval
The Great Goddess has asked a question
The matter asked about is rare even for gods
items.inference: Bhairava praises the question because it concerns knowledge difficult even for the gods to obtain.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess! You have asked me about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead
Specific syllables are mapped to bodily locations
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is placed at the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa situated within the body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
The mapping continues the sequence of bodily locations
items.inference: The syllable ṣa resides in the throat region and the syllable śa in the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the region of the throat, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows after declaring the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
Each has an associated meditation
The listener is invited to hear further
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the first divine lotus to be visualized in meditation?
premises: The lotus is divine and eight-spoked
It is adorned by the first octad
The description guides visualization
items.inference: The first meditation visualizes a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner adopt through steady meditative practice?
premises: Practice leads to an even mind
Village customs bind ordinary conduct
Renunciation of such customs is prescribed
items.inference: Through practice one should become even-minded and abandon village customs.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer to worldly or social conventions
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an even mind, one should abandon the customs of ordinary village life.

items.question: What supernatural powers arise from this meditative accomplishment?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is attained
Paralysis of bonds is attained
These are presented as results of practice
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean arresting bonds or stunning enemies
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly attributed to this practice?
premises: Immortality is mentioned as a result
Transformation is also mentioned
The teaching summarizes these briefly
items.inference: In brief, the practice grants immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam may mean bodily transformation or reversal of conditions
items.plain_english: Likewise, O Goddess, in brief one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled center characterized in meditation?
premises: A second center is introduced
It has eight petals
It is illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second eight-petaled center is well illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is the eight-petaled one, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation
Such focus enables creative power
Multiple forms can be produced
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create many forms.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the accomplished practitioner in anger?
premises: Anger activates a destructive capacity
The scope includes the entire triple world
Both moving and unmoving beings are included
items.inference: When angry, the accomplished practitioner can destroy the entire triple world with all moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is ascribed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced
It is associated with nine principles
Its function is liberation
items.inference: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava-tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles in this system
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this stage of practice?
premises: Wrinkles and grey hair are removed
Vision extends to very far distances
Both effects arise from the practice
items.inference: This practice brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the power to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

rows.grounds: object of intent; sandhi form of dhyānam

items.question: How should a solitary practitioner apply meditation to manifest multiple forms?
premises: The practice is done in solitude
The practitioner must be intent on meditation
Multiple forms are to be produced
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, the practitioner should create many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result comes from unwavering dedication to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice
Practice is continuous and dedicated
Immortality is presented as the outcome
items.inference: One intent on constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death from aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is practiced
Death associated with age is confronted
The practice leads to overcoming that death
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.
uncertainties: The exact regimen implied by divasāt nāśanena is unclear
items.plain_english: By not eating during the day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: The practice is constant yogic discipline
A duration of sixteen years is indicated
A specific bodily form is attained
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ is interpreted as the appearance of sixteen years
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from continually contemplating a smoky-colored form?
premises: A smoky-colored object is contemplated continually
Contemplation produces a causal power
The triple world can be shaken
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoky-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
uncertainties: The specific object of smoky color is not explicitly named
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoky-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
